Article Title: 'West Bengal' may soon become 'Paschim Banga'; state BJP chief says Bill coming
Article Text:
West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya says the state will soon be renamed Paschim Banga

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya on Wednesday said that the state is set to be renamed “Paschim Banga”, addint that a legislative bill would be introduced in the first session of assemby."How many times must I say, brother? The name will be 'Paschim Banga'," news agency ANI quoted him saying after he was asked about the name change again.He had also indicated earlier this week that the formal renaming was imminent, saying names such as “Paschim Bangla”, “Bangla” and “Banga” would no longer be used.“Yes, absolutely. Paschim Banga Bhavan... West Bengal's 'Paschim'... For a long time now, you will no longer have to hear names like 'Paschim Bangla', 'Bangla', or 'Banga'. 'Paschim Banga' (West Bengal) is coming,” Bhattacharya had said on Monday.Explaining the proposed legislative move, the BJP state chief said the bill would seek to link the state's official name with its historical identity.“Very soon, in the very first session itself, our government is introducing a bill so that the name of this state remains intrinsically linked with the history of this state, and that remains its identity.That is why the state is going to be named 'Paschim Banga',” he said.The proposal to rename West Bengal has a long political history. The move dates back to 1999, when the Left Front government proposed ‘Paschim Banga’ as the state's new name.The proposal was later changed to ‘Bangla’ after then Congress MLA Saugata Roy suggested it, but the Centre rejected it.After the Trinamool Congress came to power in 2011, the state again proposed ‘Paschim Banga’, which was turned down by the UPA-2 government.In 2016, the state suggested three names, ‘Bangla’ in Bengali, ‘Bengal’ in English and ‘Bangal’ in Hindi, before eventually proposing ‘Bangla’ in all three languages.In July 2018, the West Bengal assembly passed a resolution to rename the state ‘Bangla’ and sent it to the Centre for approval. However, the proposal was not cleared.The Centre cited the need for a constitutional amendment, while sources had earlier said the similarity between ‘Bangla’ and Bangladesh could cause confusion at international forums.In 2019, then Union minister of state for home Nityanand Rai told the Rajya Sabha that the Centre had not approved the name change.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya says the state is set to be renamed ‘Paschim Banga’ He adds that a legislative bill would be introduced in the first session of assemby. He had indicated earlier this week that the formal renaming was imminent.

Article Title: Delhi HC seeks Centre's response on body cameras on cops during protests
Article Text:
Delhi HC asks Centre to consider mandatory body cameras for police

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre to consider a PIL seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by police during protests and crowd-control operations, saying the issue should not be treated as a “grey area” requiring court intervention.The court asked the Centre to take a decision on the plea within six months.A bench headed by Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambhre said any direction on the use of body-worn cameras would have wider implications for policing and could not be confined to the Delhi Police alone.The bench observed while hearing the plea, “Why should we direct them to legislate? It cannot be said that it is a grey area.”The court questioned the need for judicial intervention when existing laws already provide for regulation of police procedures in areas covered by the legislature.The PIL, filed by Chahat Raghav, seeks directions for the mandatory use of body-worn cameras by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed during protests and crowd-control operations. It also seeks a comprehensive framework governing the storage, retention, integrity and evidentiary use of footage recorded by the cameras.The petitioner has cited the use of body-worn cameras by traffic police and a tender issued for their procurement, arguing that the technology is already available to the authorities.Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that body-worn cameras could enhance transparency and accountability during protests, especially in cases involving allegations of police excesses and counter-allegations against protesters.Sibal said the cameras were already being used by police in some situations, but only sporadically. He argued that the Delhi Police's 2022 standing order on rallies and demonstrations did not specifically provide for body-worn cameras and that a clear protocol was needed.He also disputed that the existing videography mechanism was sufficient, saying the recording under the standing order was different from footage captured by cameras worn directly by police personnel involved in crowd control.Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the respondents, submitted that the Delhi High Court's PIL rules require a petitioner to first approach the concerned authorities through a representation. He said the present petition could be treated as such a representation.Sharma also submitted that the Supreme Court, while hearing a matter concerning protests at Jantar Mantar, had directed the authorities to frame an SOP and that the existing mechanism already provides for videography of protests. The court recorded the ASG's statement and directed the respondents to communicate their decision on framing an SOP for the use of body-worn cameras within six months.The petitioner was given liberty to approach the High Court again in case of any inaction.The move comes amid heightened security in the New Delhi, Central Delhi and North Delhi districts following a series of demonstrations against the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed in large numbers, with multilayered barricades placed at several points to prevent protesters from entering restricted areas.
Article Summary: The Delhi High Court has asked the Centre to consider a PIL seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by police during protests and crowd-control operations. A bench headed by Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambhre said the issue should not be treated as a ‘grey area’ The court asked the centre to take a decision on the plea within six months.

Article Title: Who is Vivek Bhagat?: What is the controversy around the Delhi Police officer
Article Text:
File photo: ACP Vivek Bhagat

Who is Vivek Bhagat?

What are the allegations against him?

Why is his promotion controversial?

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police officer ACP Vivek Bhagat, currently posted as sub-divisional police officer (SDPO) in Connaught Place, has come under scrutiny after three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The complaints were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch for a “fair and impartial” enquiry. Bhagat has since consented to keeping his current duty charge as additional deputy commissioner of police on hold pending the enquiry.Bhagat is a Delhi Police officer currently serving as SDPO, Connaught Place. He was among 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP in an order approved by Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu.The Delhi government later modified the order after Bhagat formally requested that the charge concerning him be kept on hold, citing the pending Crime Branch enquiry.Bhagat had also been involved in police action during protests in June, when he was injured amid clashes between protesters and police.During those protests Bhagat said that he was allegedly surrounded and overpowered during the clashes and was beaten, kicked and punched.He reported alleged head injuries, bruises and broken teeth.An ANI report from the time said Bhagat was injured by stone and bottle pelting near Tolstoy Marg. The injuries were sustained while police were dealing with protesters during the June clashes.Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3.One journalist specifically alleged that Bhagat sexually assaulted her while she was covering the protest. She said she had approached him after noticing that no women police personnel were present while protesters were being detained.According to her complaint, she asked Bhagat about the absence of women personnel, following which he allegedly sexually assaulted and pushed her.The allegations have not been established. The Delhi Police transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements of the complainants and other people concerned.The allegations emerged just days before Bhagat was among 12 officers assigned the current duty charge of Additional DCP.A senior police officer said the promotions were routine and that the request for the promotions had been sent much earlier.After the allegations and the pending enquiry came to light, Bhagat wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner saying he consented to keeping the order concerning him on hold until the enquiry was dealt with.The Delhi government subsequently modified the administrative order, putting his Additional DCP charge on hold.The Crime Branch enquiry will determine the facts surrounding the allegations. The complaints remain allegations at this stage, and the material available does not establish that Bhagat committed sexual harassment.The Press Council of India has meanwhile expressed “shock and dismay” over the allegations and urged Delhi Police to act on the journalists’ complaints, saying journalists must be able to work without facing aggression or threats.
Article Summary: Vivek Bhagat is a Delhi Police officer currently serving as SDPO, Connaught Place. Three women journalists complained of sexual harassment following a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 3. The Delhi Police transferred the complaints to its Crime Branch, which is examining the allegations and recording statements.

Article Title: Anant Ambani unites over 50 animal welfare groups under Vantara's ‘Champions of Care’ initiative
Article Text:
"Every day, there are countless people who quietly care for animals in need, often with limited resources and little recognition, but with immense compassion,"

"Their work reminds us that kindness has no boundaries and that every life deserves care, protection and dignity. Through Champions of Care, we hope to stand alongside this work, strengthen the care available to community animals and help build a more compassionate India.

For us, this is what Every Life Matters truly means."

"I deeply appreciate Shri Anant Ambani Ji’s vision and leadership in bringing Champions of Care to life,"

"I have travelled across the world, but have rarely seen an animal care centre where such advanced facilities and technology have been made available for animals, with a level of care comparable to what we aspire to provide for people.

What touched me most was his personal effort to listen to the organisations, understand their challenges on the ground and respond with practical and sustainable solutions. By bringing these organisations together, he is not only recognising their dedication but also strengthening their collective ability to care for animals.

This is a meaningful step towards a more compassionate future for community animals across India."

A national framework for grassroots animal care

Sustainable infrastructure and nationwide collaboration

On World Animal Day, Anant Ambani, Executive Director at Reliance Industries Limited, announced 'Champions of Care', a new national initiative designed to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions.Convened at Vantara in Jamnagar, Gujarat, the landmark gathering brought together more than 50 animal welfare organisations from across India, alongside key statutory advisory members, establishing a collaborative framework to elevate animal care standards nationwide.The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys. Through targeted support in veterinary care, rescue operations, shelter facilities, and responsible population management programmes, the nationwide network is estimated to reach and support around two million animals every year.At the heart of the movement is the simple recognition that every community animal deserves care, protection, and dignity. Speaking on the launch of the initiative, Anant Ambani highlighted the unsung dedication of grassroots caregivers who work tirelessly across the country.Anant Ambani said.Eight members of the Animal Welfare Board of India (AWBI) participated in the event. S. P. Gupta, former Chairman and current member of the AWBI, commended the vision and leadership behind the nationwide drive.Gupta noted.The two-day gathering in Jamnagar provided participating delegates with an immersive experience of advanced animal care standards. Representatives toured Vantara's specialised facilities for rescued elephants and big cats, as well as naturalistic environments housing free-roaming species such as bison, zebras, and antelopes. The experience demonstrated how excellence in veterinary medicine, nutrition, housing, and lifelong care can be applied to elevate community animal welfare.Beyond facility tours, the gathering focused on connection, dialogue, and collaborative problem-solving among non-governmental organisations. A key milestone was the signing of a Letter of Understanding between Vantara and all participating organisations, formalising a shared commitment to strengthen community animal welfare. The understanding establishes a framework for knowledge sharing, capacity building, and practical support shaped by ground-level needs.Towards the close of the gathering, each participating organisation was presented with a Certificate of Appreciation signed by Anant Ambani, acknowledging their tireless devotion to animal protection.Rather than relying on short-term assistance, the initiative focuses on long-term organisational capacity and resilience. Vantara will support diverse needs identified by partner groups, including mobile veterinary services, ambulances, rescue tools, and diagnostic and treatment equipment.To help shelters become more self-sustaining and efficient, support will cover sustainable infrastructure upgrades such as solar power systems, rainwater harvesting, and improved drainage systems. Partner organisations also plan to roll out education programmes for youth, alongside quarantine and disease management infrastructure to combat infectious diseases.Conceived as an extension of Vantara's commitment to Every Life Matters, Champions of Care will continue expanding its network in the coming years, creating a connected, unified response to animal welfare across India.
Article Summary: Champions of Care is a national initiative designed to strengthen community animal welfare through practical, sustainable solutions. The initiative addresses the critical needs of community animals, including street dogs, cats, abandoned livestock, and working animals such as horses and donkeys. The nationwide network is estimated to reach and support around two million animals every year.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner (CEC) and election commissioners (ECs) should be heard by a five-judge Bench.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for the petitioners, mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and sought its listing. “We will examine and take a call,” the CJI said.The split verdict was delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. Justice Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge and opposed referring it to a larger Bench, while Justice Sharma favoured a five-judge Bench.With the two judges differing on the issue, the matter was referred to the CJI for constitution of an appropriate Bench.The top court's agreement came a day after massive protest by Rahul Gandhi-led opposition demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over poll body's special intensive revision exercise.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to examine a plea seeking recall of its September 23 split verdict. The split verdict was delivered by Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma. Justice Datta held that a two-judge Bench could hear the challenge and opposed referring it to a larger Bench.

Article Title: ‘This is merely the beginning’: Congress warns Gyanesh Kumar after INDIA bloc protest

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Pawan Khera on Tuesday warned the government that the INDIA bloc’s protest against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was only the beginning, shortly after opposition MPs were released from New Police Lines in Kingsway Camp.“The words being spoken today are going to cost them dearly. He said those in power should “mend their ways right now” and warned that the public would “bring down those who are currently riding the high horse of arrogance”.Khera named Prime Minister Narendra Modi, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Union home minister Amit Shah, saying they “will not sleep tonight—nor will they sleep soundly ever again—because they have betrayed the nation”.“If Gyanesh Kumar thinks that just because we went home today, it is all over, he needs to understand that this is merely the beginning—nothing has ended yet,” Khera said.Earlier on Tuesday, Delhi Police detained Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi along with several other Congress MPs from near Akashvani Bhavan following a day-long protest demanding the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The INDIA bloc MPs had marched from the Parliament complex towards Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission headquarters, seeking a meeting with the election commissioners over their allegations of “vote chori”.Police stopped the march near Akashvani Bhavan, following which the MPs staged a sit-in.After nearly nine hours of protest, police moved in and detained several opposition MPs, including Khera, KC Venugopal and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring. Around 50 MPs were detained and taken to New Police Lines at Kingsway Camp, according to PTI, citing sources.“The Election Commission office is barely 50 metres away, but we were not allowed to go there. I do not understand what the problem is. The Election Commission's job is to conduct elections properly. At least 300 MPs want to meet Gyanesh Kumar. But he is scared. I don't know what's happening in the country,” Rahul said.“If the representatives of the people cannot meet the Election Commission, then what is the meaning of democracy?” he said.

Article Title: Ashok Chakra for flydubai pilot Smit Machchar? Rajya Sabha MP Kartikeya Sharma urges PM Modi
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha member seeks Ashok Chakra for Indian pilot Smit Machchar

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kartikeya Sharma has written to PM Modi , urging him to consider awarding the country's highest peacetime gallantry award, the 'Ashok Chakra' to flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchar for his courage and presence of mind midair during a hijacking attempt made by Omani co-pilot.Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30 after his co-pilot attacked him and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Despite suffering severe injuries, Machchar remained focused on protecting the 174 passengers on board and continued to carry out his duties under extreme circumstances.Sharma said Machchar's courage and composure during the crisis reflected the "indomitable spirit" and dedication to duty of Indians. He said the captain put the safety of passengers ahead of his own well-being despite being seriously injured.The Rajya Sabha member said recognising Machchar at the national level would not only honour his bravery but also inspire young people across the country. He added that every Indian was proud of the captain's courage.Sharma urged Prime Minister Modi to consider conferring the 'Ashok Chakra' on Machchar in recognition of his bravery and dedication to duty.The letter comes days after the alleged hijacking attempt aboard flydubai flight FZ1073. According to reports, Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe inside the cockpit in an attempt to bring down the aircraft.Despite suffering serious injuries, Machchar managed to unlatch the cockpit door, allowing passengers and off-duty crew members to enter and restrain the co-pilot.The confrontation caused the aircraft to enter a steep descent, with the plane dropping around 16,000 feet in two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was sent.The aircraft was later diverted and made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board disembarked safely.A Times of Israel report published on Sunday said al-Hammami had planned to direct the aircraft towards Israel's Ben Gurion Airport.The report, citing Hebrew media sources, said the Omani co-pilot was detained and was being interrogated in the United Arab Emirates.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha member seeks Ashok Chakra for Indian pilot Smit Machchar. Machchar was critically injured during flydubai flight FZ1073 on September 30. Omani co- pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked Machchar with an axe.

Article Title: How will economy be impacted if India-US trade deal doesn’t happen? RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra answers
Article Text:
Malhotra’s comments come within days of FM Sitharaman indicating discussions having "reached a plateau”.

Where India-US trade deal talks stand

India’s trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible US tariffs if a trade deal does not come through, indicated RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra on Wednesday.Asked about the possible impact on the economy if the India-US trade deal is not finalised, Malhotra said, “The impact depends on what extent tariffs are going to be applied. So it's premature to answer. But obviously, it will have some negative impact.”“At the same time, we have had a number of trade agreements now in the recent past. Some of them have been operationalized, others are in the pipeline. They will help. The industry at the same time has diversified its exports,” Malhotra said at the post monetary policy press conference.“So all these things will mitigate the effect in case there is an additional tariff on some of the sectors,” he added.Also Read | Will Russian oil be economically viable for India if Trump tariffs return? Malhotra’s comments come within days of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicating that the India-US bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked, with discussions having "reached a plateau”.Sitharaman’s remarks came a few days after US Trade Representative (USTR) Jaimeson Greer indicated that an agreement was not close."I don't think there's something imminent, but we truly have identified the universe of items that are sticking points. We're working diligently toward them," he said after his meeting with Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Trump also discussed bilateral trade during a phone conversation last week, along with defence, energy and other matters.Meanwhile, Sitharaman said, “The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it," she said at the Munich Security Conference.Also Read | ‘Rate cuts off the table’: Why RBI hiked repo rate by 25 basis points but also raised GDP growth forecast to 7.1% Sitharaman said the US would look to narrow its trade deficit with India, which stood at an estimated $34 billion last year, down from $41 billion in 2024-25. The gap could reduce further as India has increased its purchases of energy from the US.Officials from India and the US have continued negotiations on the trade agreement and have repeatedly indicated that the talks were close to being concluded. The US has been pushing for greater access for its agricultural products in India through lower tariffs. However, the recent law permitting duties of up to 100% on imports of Russian oil is viewed as another hurdle in the negotiations.An agreement, in any case, can be finalised only after the Indian government has clarity on the extent of additional tariffs that could be imposed on its exports. At present, the USTR has imposed an additional duty of 10-12.5% on more than 50 countries, citing their alleged failure to prevent imports of goods produced using forced labour. The US is also examining structural overcapacity in countries including India, a charge that India has denied.In February, India and the US had agreed on a bilateral trade agreement under which the Trump administration imposed an additional 18% tariff on Indian exports. However, the arrangement was put on hold after the Supreme Court ruled that the “reciprocal tariffs” were illegal.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said India's trade agreements with other countries should help mitigate the impact of possible US tariffs if a trade deal does not come through. His comments come within days of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman indicating that the India-US bilateral trade agreement remains deadlocked.

Article Title: 'Like your movie, money is Ata Pata Laapata': SC directs Rajpal to pay Rs 2 crore by Oct 13

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore towards the amount due to the complainant in a cheque-bounce case by October 13, saying it would consider his plea against the High Court order after the payment is made.Yadav, who was present in court, brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore, while the remaining Rs 85 lakh is to be paid by October 13 through a buyer of his property, who was also present in court.The court, however, came down heavily on Yadav's conduct and warned that it could enhance his sentence, saying repeated extensions were being granted only to ensure that the complainant received the money.The Court said the deposit was directed to secure the amount due to the complainant and observed that Yadav’s conduct had not satisfied it.“Law should not be utilised like this”, the Court said.After passing the order, the bench had an informal exchange with Yadav, who spoke about the financial difficulties caused by his film Ata Pata Laapata. He said the film had resulted in losses of around Rs 200-250 crore and that the producers had also suffered losses.During the hearing, the Court also remarked in jest that the film's title was synonymous with Yadav's conduct.“Like your movie, your money is also Ata Pata Laapata, gayab”, the CJI said.Before the order was passed, film actor Rajpal Yadav appeared before the Supreme Court for the hearing of a cheque-bounce case against him and said, "The matter is before the honourable Supreme Court, and our legal team and lawyers will speak on the issue. I have the utmost respect for my country and for the Supreme Court. Whatever decision is taken by the court, wherever and whenever it is delivered, will be universally accepted. "Yadav later greeted the bench, saying, “Pranam karta hoon,” and spoke about the losses of Rs 200-250 crore he had incurred over the film.The CJI advised him to make a good film and entertain people, adding in jest that advocates appearing before the Supreme Court were also good actors and could be cast in his films.Yadav's counsel told the Court that he had approached the Registry to make the payment, but RTGS was not permissible. He said the actor had therefore brought a demand draft of Rs 1.15 crore.On the remaining Rs 85 lakh, the counsel said a buyer of Yadav's property was present in court and the amount would be paid once the transaction was completed.Yadav submitted that the dispute arose from a Rs 5 crore liability connected with the film Ata Pata Laapata, while the film had caused much larger losses.The case arises from an alleged loan extended to Yadav by Murli Projects Pvt Ltd in 2010 for Ata Pata Laapata. Seven repayment cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each were subsequently dishonoured.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore towards the amount due to the complainant in a cheque-bounce case by October 13. Article Title: Three new SC judges take oath, all in the name of God; number of women judges in SC – three out of 37
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Three new Supreme Court Judges – Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh – on Tuesday took oath of office in the name of God taking the working strength of SC to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.CJI Surya Kant administered oath to Justices Agarwal, Upadhyaya and Singh, who were chief justices of Gujarat, Delhi and Telangana HCs respectively, in the presence of SC judges, attorney general R Venkataramani, solicitor general Tushar Mehta and other senior advocates and lawyers.With the elevation of Justice Agarwal, who is the 13th women judge of SC, the strength of women judges in the apex court at present became three. The other two being Justices B V Nagarathna, who is scheduled to become the first woman CJI on Sep 24 next year, and Justice V Mohana.During the tenure of Justice N V Ramana as CJI, the Supreme Court had the highest number of sitting SC judges at four – Justices India Banerjee, Nagarathna, Hima Kohli and Bela M Trivedi, last three of whom had taken oath on Aug 31, 2021. While the Collegium led by Justice Ramana had recommended appointment of three women judges, the present collegium led by CJI Kant has so far appointed two women judges.SC got its first woman judge in M Fathima Beevi on Oct 6, 1989, 39 years after SC was established. Justice Beevi had retired from Kerala HC on Apr 29, 1989, but was elevated to the SC five months after retirement. Other women judges in SC were – Justices Sujata V Manohar, Ruma Pal, Gyan Sudha Misra, Ranjana P Desai, R Bhanumathi and Indu Malhotra.SC judge strength was increased from 34 to 38, including the CJI, initially through an Ordinance on May 16. The corresponding Amendment Act was passed by Parliament which received the President's assent on Aug 11. In Aug 2019, during the tenure of CJI Ranjan Gogoi, the sanctioned strength of SC judges was increased from 31 to 34, including CJI.The SC had started in 1950 with a sanctioned strength of 8 Judges, which was increased to 11 in 1956, 14 in 1960, 18 in 1978, 26 in 1986, and 31 in 2009. SC as of Tuesday has a pendency of 95, 481 cases.
Article Summary: Three new Supreme Court Judges – Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh – on Tuesday took oath of office in the name of God. The working strength of SC to 37 judges, just one short of the sanctioned strength.

Article Title: Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
Article Text:
File photo: Sugarcane at a market, in Guwahati

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) starting November, amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season and indications of a further decline in output due to drought in major sugarcane-growing states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.TOI has learnt that government will notify the decision soon, ahead of the start of the new ESY. While ethanol supply year runs from Nov 1 to Oct 31, sugar season in India runs from Oct 1 to Sep 30. Government specifies the quantity of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses that can be diverted for ethanol production to meet the mandatory blending target for the green fuel in petrol.The move comes at a time when domestic sugar supplies remain tight. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol production during the sugar season that ended on September 30. The new sugar season began on October 1 with opening stocks of around 37.5 lakh tonnes, compared with nearly 50 lakh tonnes a year ago.Industry sources said there was no scope for allowing further diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol, as ensuring adequate domestic sugar supplies remains a priority for both govt and mills.With the possibility of a fall in output in the current season, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, government would prioritise sugar availability over additional diversion for ethanol.Disallowing the use of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol in 2026-27 would enable mills to produce more sugar from the available cane, helping augment domestic supplies and meeting consumption requirements.Government has said that the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Besides, nearly three-fourths of ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize, reducing the dependence on sugar-based feedstock.“Meeting the demand for 20% ethanol blending in petrol won’t be an issue. With indications of millers getting a better price, it won’t be a problem for them either. Government would have to continue with the ban on exports and may have to allow more imports as well,” an industry analyst said.Sugar production in the 2025-26 season was hit by crop diseases, waterlogging and adverse weather in key producing states. Against the initial production estimate of around 343 lakh tonnes, output was estimated at around 306 lakh tonnes in August, including the quantity diverted for ethanol production.After accounting for the diversion to ethanol, net sugar production in 2025-26 was around 279 lakh tonnes, barely enough to meet the normative domestic consumption requirement of 280-285 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) The move comes amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol during the sugar season that ended on September 30.

On October 7, 2001, when I took the oath as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, I had not imagined that this milestone, too, would arrive.

The people have always chosen me to serve them. Today, I pay tribute to India's democracy and its Constitution. ! Global Manufacturing hub! Hosting of the Olympics! Stepping into Space! This energy and confidence are incredible. I sincerely believe that every citizen of India has foremost claim on me. Article Title: 'Beyond limits': Ex-CJI Gavai, former judges slam SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks amid EC-SIR row
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission.Gavai said that a sitting judge should not have made comments on the ongoing row over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls as the matter is sub judice before the top court."Judicial propriety would not permit him to make any comment on the matter which is sub judice before the court," Gavai told news agency PTI.Retired Delhi high court judges SN Dhingra and RS Sodhi also questioned Bhuyan's remarks.Justice Dhingra said Bhuyan's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" and such comments should not be made at a public event when the issue is pending before the same court."He should have thought a thousand times before making such a statement," Dhingra said, adding that Justice Bhuyan did not know the full facts of the issue.Justice R S Sodhi also criticised Justice Bhuyan for calling the SIR exercise disenfranchisement and said that the right to vote was governed by the statutory framework."Whether you have a vote or you don't have a vote depends upon the statute. If you fall within the parameters of the statute, you have a vote.If you don't fall within the parameters of the statute, you don't have a vote," Justice Sodhi said."I mean, these hardline thinking and these hardline statements, to my mind, are not a very mature way of looking at a thing, especially when you are supposed to be in a field which is supposed to be excellent in its rationalising," he said.This comes a day after Justice Bhuyan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary" and a "negation" of the constitutional order.While delivering the valedictory address at the 19th Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court Competition at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Justice Bhuyan said that the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, one with voting rights and the other without voting rights, and no amount of "whataboutery" could justify such a process.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.This is not the first time that Justice Bhuyan has put forth his views on issues being discussed in the public domain.Recently, NALSAR Hyderabad was in the news after a section of its students wrote to the vice chancellor, registrar and professors of the institution, opposing any proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest to the varsity's convocation.Justice Bhuyan, who served as the Chancellor of NALSAR, on Sunday said he can be legitimately proud of the students of the institution."You have shown to the country and the world what a university student, that too, a student of law, should be like. You are brilliant. You are bold and you are brave," he said.
Article Summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai and other retired judges on Monday condemned Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan's remarks on the Election Commission. Justice Dhingra and RS Sodhi said Bhuya's statement was "way beyond the limits of a sitting top court judge" This comes a day after Justice Bhuayan said that any process that "disenfranchises" millions of Indian citizens was "intrinsically arbitrary"

Article Title: CBI raids CM Bhagwant Mann’s camp office, his OSD’s home in graft probe
Article Text:
Central forces stand guard as CBI searches Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann's camp office in Chandigarh

After CBI raid in graft probe, Punjab CM claims BJP has started poll preparation

NEW DELHI/CHANDIGARH: CBI registered an FIR against Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s OSD Rajbir Ghuman and five others Tuesday, following it up with raids on eight locations, including the CM’s camp office in Chandigarh.The coordinated search came within hours of the state govt moving Supreme Court against Punjab and Haryana high court’s order for a CBI probe into ED’s allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through the OSD.The search at Mann’s camp office in House No 50 of Sector 2 started around 6pm, sending shockwaves through the administration. It was at this office that Ghuman used to allegedly meet the co-accused, said CBI sources. A CBI team also visited Ghuman’s home in his village, Gharachon in Sangrur.CBI said the case was registered following a court order that was based on an ED report. The investigation centres on allegations of corruption and abuse of power and political influence. Apart from Ghuman, those named by CBI in the FIR are Nitin Gohal, Jitin Gohal alias Raja, Romi Raja Mahajan, Bir Devinder, RS Nagra and “unknown public servant(s) and private person(s)”.Nitin is alleged to be a “liaison” in the “cash-for-transfer” scandal with access to Ghuman. His brother Jitin was allegedly provided access to CMO through Ghuman and Dr Romi Mahajan, described as an “associate” who allegedly worked with Ghuman and helped coordinate appointments. Devinder is an AAP youth activist and Nagra is a “private associate”.CBI searched premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar and seized laptops, mobile phones and financial documents.The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery, official impropriety, and financial paper trails.Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann responded through a post on X in Punjabi, “BJP has started preparations for Punjab elections. A CBI raid was conducted at my camp office. Now ED and CBI will be misused in Punjab so that Punjab govt and I can be defamed. BJP is in panic as it sees the love received from people.”CBI said the FIR is meant to investigate allegations of corruption against OSD to CM, Rajbir Ghuman, and his associates for “influencing and manipulating postings of officers, including that of IAS and IPS officers, departmental proceedings, matters pertaining to policy formulation, administrative approvals, tender conditions, licensing matters, land use conversion matters, property disputes, revenue and land-related issues in lieu of pecuniary benefits”.“It is also alleged that the accused public servants purportedly accessed and provided drafts of orders and policies to private persons prior to their issuance by the govt,” said CBI, adding that those named in the FIR include two public servants, middlemen, and associates.ED had conducted searches in Punjab from May 7-10 in a PMLA case and written to the DGP on July 30 to register a case.Advocate Nikhil Saraf filed a PIL in HC, alleging ED had written three letters to the Punjab DGP, seeking registration of an FIR against Ghuman and others, yet Punjab Police didn’t do so.On Monday, a division bench of Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor heard the PIL and said, “We are not impressed by the manner in which Punjab Police has acted so far and, therefore, deem it appropriate to entrust investigation to CBI.”
Article Summary: CBI searches premises linked to the accused in Chandigarh, Mohali, Gurdaspur, Ludhiana, Patiala, Sangrur and Jalandhar. The seized laptops, mobile phones and documents are currently undergoing forensic scrutiny to establish evidence of bribery and official impropriety.

Article Title: Modi's 25 years in office: A study in seva and action

(The writer is the president, Shri Ram Chandra Mission, Global Guide of Heartfulness Meditation)

In a democracy, when someone completes 25 consecutive years as the head of a govt, it is indeed special. I heartily congratulate Shri Narendra Modi ji on 25 glorious years of service as head of govt. He is someone I am very fond of and someone I have interacted with closely over the years.Who is Modiji? What makes him successful? What drives him? These are very common questions and are worth pondering over.For me, Prime Minister Modi is a blend of both leadership and spirituality.When I reflect upon the life of Narendrabhai, one quality that draws my attention is this sense of an underlying purpose running through very different phases of his life. I have often spoken of the divided heart - a heart pulled in many directions by competing desires. There is an inherent tension between freedom and desire, between what is pleasant and what is good. Aspirants on the spiritual path encounter this tension and have to work at resolving it before real progress is possible.In Narendrabhai's life, we can see that this work happened quite early on. I recently learned that at seventeen, he left home, travelled across India and spent time in the Himalayas; influenced by Swami Vivekananda and his encounters with different communities and traditions, his life began to orient itself towards service.Thereafter, the outer form kept changing - from pracharak to organiser, from CM to PM, but the idea of service remained a recurring thread. When the heart becomes united in purpose, positions cease to be destinations in themselves. They become different instruments through which that purpose can find expression.The devastating flood at Morbi in 1979, following failure of the Machchhu dam, gave this commitment a demanding field of action. Narendrabhai worked there as a volunteer in the aftermath of disaster. Years later, while visiting landslide-affected Wayanad in 2024, he recalled that experience as helping him understand suffering of families who'd lost so much. When we serve people in their hour of distress, their difficulties cease to be concerns. They become responsibilities we feel within ourselves.A sense of purpose finds expression in the way we respond to the person before us. When Seva takes root in the heart, even an ordinary encounter becomes an opportunity to care. An incident from Narendrabhai's earlier life brings this quality to mind.In her account "A train journey and two names to remember," published in The Hindu in 2014, Leena Sarma recalled her journey from Delhi to Ahmedabad in 1990 with Utpalparna Hazarika. Both women were Railway Traffic Service probationers, travelling for the next phase of training without confirmed berths. The ticket examiner found them space in a first-class compartment occupied by Narendra Modi and Shankersinh Vaghela. That evening, Narendrabhai paid for all four vegetarian meals. Later, when the ticket examiner explained that no berths could be arranged for the women, both men surrendered theirs, spread a cloth on the floor and slept there, leaving the berths to the two probationers.What touches me is the ease with which they gave up their comfort. In Sarma's recollection, the kindness came without ceremony. This was long before Narendrabhai became chief minister or Prime Minister, and the need before him was simple and immediate. Such moments invite us to reflect on how we behave when no one is watching as an example of leadership. Can we notice another person's difficulty and respond without seeking recognition? To me, this is generosity of heart. It gives a human warmth to purpose and allows seva to become part of everyday life.Doubt will visit every sincere seeker, just as uncertainty accompanies every person who accepts a great responsibility. If one listens to its whisperings, faith is progressively fractured; the will loses its ability to drive action and real spiritual progress becomes difficult. The question is not whether doubt arises, but whether we allow it to become the driver of our lives. This is where shraddha becomes so important.Shraddha is more than belief; it contains trust, self-confidence, sincerity, determination and inner conviction. I am reminded here of Narendrabhai becoming CM of Gujarat in 2001. At fifty-one, he had never contested an election and had never held an administrative position. He was asked to govern a state still recovering from a devastating earthquake and there were understandable questions about whether an experienced organiser could become an effective administrator. Yet he accepted the responsibility and learnt while carrying it. His early tenure as chief minister was fraught with many challenges that he had to overcome, challenges that could have tested the faith of many.Conviction does not mean that we know beforehand that we will succeed. It means that uncertainty does not prevent us from taking the next step. We may hear the voice of doubt, we may learn from it, but we need not hand over to it the direction of our lives. Narendrabhai's life is one where doubt has never been allowed into the driver's seat; in fact, courage and conviction have been given that place.Fear asks, "What if?" while faith responds, "Even if." Fearlessness does not mean that a human being never experiences fear. What matters is whether fear is permitted to determine our direction. Narendrabhai's life offers examples of accepting responsibility in very different circumstances of uncertainty. In his mid-sixties, when Narendrabhai accepted the mantle of being Prime Minister of India, the scale of uncertainty was enormous: he moved from leading one state to assuming responsibility for India's national security, diplomacy and relationships with the world, at a time when questions were being asked about how a state leader would make that transition.Later came a spell of challenges that may constitute one of the most turbulent periods in recent history. The Covid pandemic, trade wars, the geopolitical upheaval following the war in Ukraine and the recent West Asia crisis, along with domestic challenges, feature among circumstances that would have tested the fortitude of any leader, let alone one who holds the hopes of 1.4 billion. To navigate this with poise is exemplary. Perhaps this is one way of understanding courage spiritually. It is not to say, "Nothing can happen to me." It is to say, "Whatever may happen, I will not allow fear alone to decide what I must do."And so, for any student of leadership, there is a clear lesson from his life. Cultivating a heart free from division, allowing generosity to guide our actions, anchoring mind in conviction and developing a spirit that does not act from fear are spiritual principles that have helped shape Narendrabhai's path as a karmayogi. These principles are universal and when we see them manifest in someone's life, we can use them as inspiration.I take this occasion to wish Narendrabhai all the very best; may the divine grant him a long life to carry forward this era with leadership and guidance, and may he continue to take India to greater and greater heights.
Article Summary: Shri Ram Chandra Mission president congratulates Narendra Modi on 25 years as head of govt. He says Modi is a blend of both leadership and spirituality. Modi has a sense of an underlying purpose running through very different phases of his life, he says.

Article Title: 'Unable to distinguish between victim & perpetrator': India tears into OIC over J&K remarks at UN
Article Text:
Biplab Deb counters OIC over J&K, terror remarks

NEW DELHI: India hit back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly, rejecting its remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and New Delhi’s actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.West Tripura Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb, delivering India’s national statement at the UNGA Sixth Committee on Tuesday said the OIC had failed to distinguish between those responsible for terrorism and its victims.“I also address now the statement delivered by the chair of the OIC on India's focused and measured actions against terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, from where terrorist attacks against India were planned and directed,” news agency PTI quoted Deb saying.He added that it is “regrettable that those delivering the statement” are “unable to separate fact from fiction and distinguish between victim and perpetrator”.India asserted that it has the right to defend its citizens against cross-border terrorism and warned that there would be consequences for those who engage in terrorism.Deb also objected to what he called the OIC’s “unwarranted reference” to Jammu and Kashmir.He urged the grouping to instead focus on Pakistan’s “illegal occupation” and alleged rights violations in PoK.“The OIC chair would do better to focus on Pakistan's illegal occupation, especially in Rawalakot, where wanton killings, brutal violence and the denial of basic rights to the people living there are so visible. Such willful blindness only speaks of bigotry and intolerance,” he said.Saudi Arabia had delivered the OIC statement at the Sixth Committee, which deals with legal issues. The OIC referred to “military escalation in Southeast Asia” and “unjustified strikes” at multiple locations in Pakistan, without naming India.India’s response came as it reiterated its position that cross-border terrorism remains a persistent threat. Deb cited the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, in which 26 civilians were killed, and said the attack demonstrated the human cost of terrorism.“The Pahalgam terror attack was a calculated assault on our sovereignty, planned and executed by networks that continue to enjoy state patronage, safe havens, and material and logistical support from across our western border,” he said.Deb also called terrorism one of the gravest threats to international peace and security, stressing that there could be no justification for attacks on civilians.“Terrorism is antithetical to the values of the UN. There can be no justification whatsoever for deliberately targeting civilians. There is no distinction between good and bad terrorism,” he said.
Article Summary: India hits back at the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) at the UN General Assembly. West Tripura Lok Sabha MP Biplab Kumar Deb said the OIC had failed to distinguish between those responsible for terrorism and its victims. He urged the grouping to instead focus on Pakistan’s “illegal occupation” and alleged rights violations in PoK.

Article Title: 'Inflation man Modi's reign of terror continues': Congress on repo rate hike
Article Text:
Congress slams Centre after RBI raises repo rate to 5.5%

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Wednesday attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, saying the move would further increase the financial burden on the public.Calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi “inflation man”, the Congress said, “Inflation Man Modi's reign of terror continues. Now the public's back will be broken even further.”The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans, resulting in higher EMIs and potentially longer repayment periods. “To curb inflation as per Modi's intent, the RBI has today raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%,” it said."This means your home loan, car loan, personal loan, and business loan interest rates will now increase. Now you'll have to pay higher EMIs, and the loan repayment period will also get extended. The promise was of 'good days,' but what we got were days of extortion," he added.The RBI's monetary policy committee unanimously approved the hike and shifted its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening, citing stronger-than-expected economic growth and broader price pressures.The rate increase would raise the monthly EMI on a Rs 1 crore home loan with a 15-year tenure by around Rs 1,500, assuming a base rate of 8.50%. If borrowers keep their EMI unchanged, the higher interest rate could extend the repayment period by roughly six instalments.The RBI also raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1%, while increasing its inflation projection by 20 basis points to 5.2%. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said stronger capacity utilisation, bank credit growth, government capital expenditure and infrastructure spending were supporting investment and demand.CPI inflation rose to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July. Malhotra said price pressures had broadened beyond volatile items, with food inflation becoming more widespread, including higher sugar and onion prices.The Congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”.
Article Summary: The Congress attacked the Centre after the Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. The party said the rate hike would push up borrowing costs for home, car, personal and business loans. The Congress said the government's promise of “good days” had instead delivered “days of extortion”

Article Title: KPSC recruitment case: Suspended chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, member BV Geetha detained
Article Text:
KPSC Case: ED Arrests Suspended Chairman Sahukar, Member Geetha

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Tuesday detained suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and KPSC member BV Geetha after conducting searches at Sahukar's residence in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar.Last week, the ED completed questioning suspended IAS officer and former KPSC controller of examinations Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar after taking him into custody. Another accused in the case, self-styled political activist Basavaraj Kannale, was also questioned by the agency. Both Gangwar and Kannale are currently in judicial custody at Bengaluru Central Prison after their bail pleas were rejected by the courts.On Tuesday morning, a team of ED officials reached Sahukar's residence and recorded his statement. He was detained later in the evening. Another ED team picked up KPSC member BV Geetha from her flat in an apartment in Dollars Colony, Sanjaynagar, for questioning.The ED had earlier recorded statements from several candidates, including Suguresh, a close relative of Sahukar who had secured unusually high marks, according to the FIR.Sources said Sahukar was detained based on Suguresh's confession.The investigation has also found that Sahukar allegedly called Gangwar twice on the night of January 7, a day before the examination. Gangwar is accused of sharing the question paper and an answer script with Suguresh, who allegedly later shared them with Geetha.Sahukar, a native of Hemanala village in Raichur district's Devadurga taluk, holds a degree in Agricultural Engineering. He was appointed as a KPSC member in September 2019 and was elevated as chairman in April 2021 by then governor Vajubhai Vala on the recommendation of the state government, succeeding Shadakshari Swamy.Sahukar has also faced scrutiny in a separate case involving allegations that his daughter submitted a fraudulent income certificate showing an annual family income of Rs 40,000 to claim reservation under Category 3B for government employment.The Karnataka High Court had criticised the declaration as a "fraud" and an "eyewash", observing that Sahukar was drawing a substantial salary as KPSC chairman. He was subsequently suspended from office following cabinet recommendations.He is also under investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over alleged irregularities, paper leaks and cash-for-jobs cases linked to recruitment examinations, including the recruitment of 400 veterinary officers and other gazetted posts.The investigations have alleged the involvement of middlemen and illegal transactions in exchange for candidate selections. His anticipatory bail plea was earlier rejected by the High Court after the CID presented evidence allegedly linking him and his associates to middlemen.The ED is investigating the money-laundering aspects of the alleged recruitment scams and has conducted searches as part of its probe into the financial trail and suspected illicit assets.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) detained suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) chairman Shivashankarappa S Sahukar and KPSC member BV Geetha. The ED is investigating the money-laundering aspects of the alleged recruitment scams and has conducted searches as part of its probe.

Article Title: 'Congress loses even on ballot papers': Himanta hails NDA's Silchar civic polls victory

BJP-led NDA sweeps first Silchar civic polls with 34 seats

NEW DELHI: The ruling BJP-led NDA won the first elections to the Silchar Municipal Corporation on Tuesday, securing 34 of the 42 seats.Reacting to the result, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said Congress performs poorly even when elections are held through paper ballots.“See, Congress loses even on paper ballots. In fact, Congress loses even more on paper ballots. That’s why in EVMs, sometimes people go and press NOTA or get panicked seeing the machine and vote in the wrong place. But people are well-practiced in voting on paper ballots. So whenever voting happens on paper ballots, Congress loses even more,” Sarma said.Polling for the 40 wards was held on October 3, while BJP candidates Bijendra Prasad Singh and Bhakti Sen Talukdar were elected unopposed from wards 9 and 20, respectively. Counting of votes began at 8 am, with ballot papers used in the elections.Sarma said the verdict reflected the people's faith in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership and his vision for urban governance under the Viksit Bharat initiative."Another day, another win for @BJP4Assam! The people of Silchar have given us a thumping majority in the Silchar Municipal Corporation elections, held through BALLOT PAPER," Sarma said in a post on X.He thanked the people of Silchar for the “resounding mandate” and reiterated his government's commitment to making the city “one of Assam's foremost cities”.Assam BJP president Dilip Saikia said the results showed that Congress had failed to win public support even in an election conducted through ballot papers."The Congress always complains about EVM tampering, but this election was held through ballot papers, and they are nowhere," he told reporters.The BJP won 32 seats, while its ally Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) secured two. The BJP has sought recounting in two wards, 29 and 30, where an Independent candidate and a Congress candidate, respectively, emerged victorious. A decision on the demand is yet to be taken, they said.A total of 133 candidates contested the elections. The BJP fielded candidates in 38 wards, the AGP in four and the Congress in 38, while 52 Independents and one CPI(M) candidate were also in the fray.The Silchar Municipal Board was upgraded to a 42-ward municipal corporation in 2022 and became operational in June 2025. Silchar, the principal city of the Barak Valley, had remained without an elected civic body for six years.Poor road conditions, inadequate drainage, waterlogging, erratic power supply and irregular drinking water supply were among the key issues raised during the campaign.

Article Title: From Gujarat CM to India's PM: Narendra Modi's 25 years in office
Article Text:
A push for manufacturing semiconductors as well as for startups and self-reliance, continues to be Modi’s focus in his third term as PM

Oct 2001-May 2014: Gujarat CM

Kutch rebuilt. In 2003, Gujarat passed India's first state disaster management law.

Vibrant Gujarat Summit launched in 2003 to showcase its strength & attract investors.

Jyotigram Yojana, launched in 2006, prioritised reliable power supply over subsidised but erratic electricity to villages. Soon, all 18,000 villages had access to reliable three-phase power as non-farm economic activity expanded and subsidies were nearly halved.

Sagarkhedu Sarvangi Vikas Yojana launched in 2007 adopted an outcome-oriented mission for coastal communities, combining infrastructure, livelihoods, irrigation, salinity control, coastal security and fisheries development.

Launched in 2009, Garib Kalyan Mela took welfare delivery to citizens.

Check dams, farm ponds, recharge wells, canals and inter-basin transfers were planned as surplus floodwater was carried through 332km of canals and Narmada water reached reservoirs across Saurashtra, opening over 10 lakh acres of irrigation potential. A CAG report in 2017 recorded groundwater recharge roughly 50% above 2002 levels.

His government linked ports with power, roads, rail and industrial estates. Mundra, Hazira and Pipavav grew into major private ports.

2014-2019: First term as PM

His government launched Jan Dhan Yojana, and 59 crore accounts were opened with over Rs 3.1 lakh crore in deposits. Women owned 33 crore of these accounts. This helped in ushering in direct benefit transfer, changing welfare delivery. By Aug 2026, DBT had transferred Rs 53.2 lakh crore across 320 schemes and 56 ministries.

In his Aug 15 speech at Red Fort, Modi spoke of the indignities women suffer due to lack of toilets and announced a sanitation campaign. Swachh Bharat Mission was launched. PM Ujjwala Yojana, launched in 2016, gave 10.5 crore free LPG connections to women from poor households by May 2026.

His government expanded the social security net, including free treatment for the poor under Ayushman Bharat. By 2025, official estimates say 94.3 crore Indians were covered by some form of social protection, up from 19% in 2015 to 64%.

GST was rolled out in July 2017 in what the PM lauded as economic unification of India as tax borders came down and the market became one.



2019-24: Second term as PM

Few people outside the top echelons of government were aware when it took probably its most significant political calls: revoking the special constitutional status enjoyed by J&K under Article 370, downgrading the state to the status of UT and hiving off Ladakh as a UT.

A verdict from SC paved the way for construction of Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. The idol was consecrated in Jan 2024.

CAA was passed in 2019, providing a path to citizenship for persecuted non-Muslim communities from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.

The Covid pandemic and lockdowns tested government as India suffered a large human toll. Scaling up of indigenous vaccines and the world's largest vaccination campaign helped. Government launched the Atmanirbhar Bharat programme. It was also a period when UPI use began zooming and has become a definitive success.

2024: Wins a third term

Narendra Modi was thrust into the thick of governance in 2001 as the party suffered a setback in local polls in Gujarat and the response of the state government headed by CM Keshubhai Patel to the massive Kutch earthquake was found wanting.Within months of his swearing-in as CM, riots swept the state in the wake of the Godhra train-burning incident. BJP's win in the 2002 assembly polls cemented his position and dissidents in the party were marginalised as he set about implementing his governance agenda.Nudged by RSS, the BJP brass named Modi in June 2013 as its campaign committee head for the 2014 polls and soon elevated him as its PM candidate. When results were announced on May 16, BJP more than doubled its tally to 282, its first majority in the then 545-member Lok Sabha. It was the first majority government since 1984.BJP went into the 2024 elections with supreme confidence and was humbled as a section of voters balked at its "abki baar 400 paar" slogan. However, it won a majority with its allies even as it lost its own majority after a decade.A manufacturing push in semiconductors, startups and self-reliance continues to be the focus. Govt cited India's high growth rate to emphasise handling of global headwinds.Security forces' success in virtually eliminating Naxalism, cited by predecessor Manmohan Singh as the biggest internal threat to India, has been a boost to BJP's national security agenda.Operation Sindoor targeted terrorist hideouts in Pakistan in May 2025 after the Pahalgam attack.
Article Summary: Narendra Modi was thrust into the thick of governance in 2001 as the party suffered a setback in local polls in Gujarat. His government launched Jan Dhan Yojana, and 59 crore accounts were opened with over Rs 3.1 lakh crore in deposits. Swachh Bharat Mission was launched.

Article Title: Punjab government moves Supreme Court against CBI probe into 'bribe syndicate' linked to CM Bhagwant Mann's OSD
Article Text:
Supreme Court said the state’s petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday

NEW DELHI: Hours before CBI carried out searches at Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann 's camp office in Chandigarh and registered an FIR against his OSD and others, Punjab govt had rushed Supreme Court to urgently hear its appeal against Punjab and Haryana HC's Monday order directing the agency to probe ED's allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through an OSD in the CM's office.Fearing imminent coercive action - based on the HC order for registration of an FIR - by CBI against top politicians and bureaucrats in the state, the Mann-led AAP govt in its appeal sought an urgent stay of the HC's directions. "If the impugned judgement is not stayed, CBI will register an FIR against high public functionaries of the state on untested material... and the situation will become irreversible," it said.Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the state govt, said HC had brushed aside the state's preliminary objections, declined three weeks to Punjab Police to complete the preliminary inquiry, which it initiated based on ED's communication levelling "cash-for-transfers postings" allegation, and directed a CBI probe, contrary to the federal scheme of governance mandated by the Constitution."Please hear the petition today itself at 2pm," Singh requested a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.When the bench said it was impossible to take the appeal for hearing Tuesday itself, Singh said the appeal must be heard Wednesday, suggesting the development can have potentially a huge political fallout in the poll-bound state and arguing that the order marked a breach of the federal scheme of governance.The bench said the state's petition will be listed for hearing either Wednesday or Thursday.In its appeal, the state govt revealed ED's Jalandhar zonal office on July 30 sent a 150-page communication to Punjab DGP under PMLA, alleging it was found that one Nihal Gohal, whose premises were searched in May, influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions "through an officer on special duty in the office of CM".DGP marked the communication, large parts of which were illegible, to Punjab Bureau of Investigation on Aug 3. The bureau began its preliminary inquiry within two days and started collecting evidence from different departments. It sent reminders to ED on Aug 28, Sept 2 and Sept 5, asking it to depute an officer with complete records, but no cooperation was received till Sept 7, the state claimed.HC had ordered a CBI probe because of what it held to be inaction in the registeration of an FIR on the material evidence sent by ED and had said, "Prima facie allegations with regard to scams including cash for transfers, cash for getting favourable policies, cash for tenders, and such other illegal activities corruption in high public offices have been substantiated by ED with reference to various WhatsApp chats and other information. .."Punjab govt said the high court erred by sending CBI into a state which had withdrawn consent to the agency needed to carry out an investigation in the state's jurisdiction, without citing any exceptional circumstances that warranted a CBI probe.In 2010, SC had ruled that SC and HCs can direct a CBI probe in exceptional cases even in states which have withdrawn general consent.
Article Summary: Punjab govt rushed Supreme Court to urgently hear its appeal against Punjab and Haryana HC's Monday order directing the agency to probe ED's allegation that a bribe syndicate influenced transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions through an OSD in the CM's office. HC had ordered a CBI probe because of what it held to be inaction in the registeration of an FIR.

Article Title: ED unearths bribe racket involving top executives of 40 PSUs, banks & companies

NEW DELHI: Enforcement Directorate has unearthed a bribery racket involving top executives of at least 40 public sector undertakings and government banks, besides some corporate houses engaged in siphoning off and laundering hundreds of crores of corporate social responsibility (CSR) funds channelled through multiple charities promoted by a class XII dropout, who has been caught impersonating as a medical doctor for close to three decades.According to ED, the fake doctor, Dharmendra Kumar Chandradev, received CSR donations in his multiple trusts registered for the purpose of laundering money meant for charity and exempted from taxation. These funds were further returned back to the "donor" in cash, after retaining his commission. The racket involved some corporate houses, hospitals, public sector companies and govt banks. Top executives of these PSUs were heavily bribed for releasing CSR funds.On Oct 1, the central agency carried out searches at eight locations across Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and Delhi-NCR related to these bogus donations cases. The agency seized several pieces of evidence and details of transactions related to PSU executives and corporate hospitals, in addition to Rs 21 lakh in unaccounted cash."The CSR mechanism was utilised as a conduit for conversion of accounted funds into unaccounted cash.Funds amounting to Rs 200 crore have been routed through the above mechanism," ED has estimated through its preliminary investigation.The agency further said its probe revealed that CSR contributions from corporate houses were "returned substantially in cash" to the contributors after deduction of a small commission.Searches have also revealed a network of agents and intermediaries who channelled CSR funds to the trusts, which were thereafter routed through shell entities controlled by market operators. Most of these entities have also been flagged in multiple GST fraud investigations."At least 40 PSUs and public sector banks across the country have provided CSR donations to the trusts operated by the accused. Several projects were only partially executed or not executed in proportion to the funds received, while vendor bills were inflated and excess funds routed through bogus or shell entities. Kickbacks and commissions were allegedly paid to intermediaries facilitating the CSR funding," ED said.
Article Summary: The racket involved some corporate houses, hospitals, public sector companies and govt banks. Top executives of these PSUs were heavily bribed for releasing CSR funds. On Oct 1, the central agency carried out searches at eight locations across Maharashtra, Bengal, Gujarat and Delhi-NCR.

Article Title: Election Commission: Was ready to meet 240 opposition MPs but not at their chosen venue
Article Text:
Till 4 pm, no political party had sought an appointment, EC said

NEW DELHI: Election Commission on Tuesday, while willing to meet the 240 opposition party MPs at their request conveyed through Delhi Police, declined to do so at their suggested venue of Parliament House annexe, saying the poll panel's protocol required such meetings to be held only on EC premises and based on a request from the parties' authorised representative."EC considered this request as unusual and therefore, it could not be accepted," the panel said in a statement.As an alternative, EC proposed that its most senior officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive a memorandum, "which in itself would have been an unprecedented step", said an EC spokesperson. However, this offer was declined by the MPs.While emphasising that any political party may request for a meeting with EC, which would then schedule a date and time, the commission said it must balance its respect for parliamentary and democratic processes with that for its own protocols and conventions, "which are of utmost importance".EC said during the march by certain political parties towards Nirvachan Sadan, "it was learnt through the media that some MPs wished to meet the commission along with their delegation"."It is clarified that, till 4pm, no political party, through its representatives, had sought an appointment for a meeting with EC," the commission said. EC said around 4pm, information was received from police that a delegation of MPs led by Rahul Gandhi wished to meet and submit a memorandum.Referring to the procedure laid down in 2025 for meetings with political parties, EC said if a delegation wishes to meet, it seeks an appointment through its authorised representative. The meeting is thereafter held at a time mutually agreed upon by both sides. "This is a regular practice," EC said.When the panel was considering the proposal, it was informed by the Delhi Police DCP that the meeting was sought to be held with 240 MPs and the proposed venue was the Parliament House annexe, it said. "EC, considering its protocol to meet political parties only on its own premises and its procedure to only schedule such meetings in consultation with the parties' authorised representative, declined the offer," it said.
Article Summary: Election Commission was willing to meet the 240 opposition party MPs at their request conveyed through Delhi Police. But it declined to do so at their suggested venue of Parliament House annexe. The poll panel's protocol required such meetings to be held only on EC premises and based on a request from the parties' authorised representative.

NEW DELHI: Cabinet on Tuesday adopted a resolution hailing the achievements of Narendra Modi in the last 25 years, first as chief minister of Gujarat and subsequently as PM.I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution marks Modi's uninterrupted public service between Oct 7, 2001 and Oct 7, 2026. The resolution listed decisions taken by Modi which have touched the lives of common man and has given the country confidence. Vaishnaw said Modi's success and long service is a result of people's trust and faith in his style of governance and a vibrant example of the strength of Indian democracy.The resolution highlighted PM's tenure with a list of policy and political mandate he has got in Gujarat and at Centre. It mentioned initiatives from Modi's tenure as Gujarat CM that were adopted and extended at the national level. These included SWAGAT, the grievance-redressal system through which Modi interacted with citizens in Gujarat, and PRAGATI, Centre's platform for reviewing major projects and resolving implementation hurdles.It also cited Gujarat's Jyotigram scheme, which created separate agricultural electricity feeders, as an approach subsequently expanded nationally. The resolution linked Modi's experience of poverty with welfare initiatives, citing 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts, over 4 crore homes and 25 crore people moving out of poverty.It highlighted women's empowerment, saying nearly 3.5 crore women had become Lakhpati Didis, while Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam provided for women's reservation.PM-KISAN transfers exceeding Rs 4 lakh crore and PM-JANMAN for vulnerable tribal groups were also cited.
Article Summary: I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the resolution marks Modi's uninterrupted public service between October 7, 2001 and Oct 7, 2026. The resolution listed decisions taken by Modi which have touched the lives of common man and has given the country confidence.

JAMMU: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones in the border village of Arnia in Jammu district. An Italy-made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches, police said Tuesday.On Oct 3, cops manning a checkpoint at Arnia’s Tamala Bridge stopped two men moving on a bike around 10.45pm. One of the men, Rahul Kumar, was found carrying 264g of suspected heroin, a Beretta pistol, two magazines and four live rounds. Another 276g of suspected heroin was seized from the second man, Ajay Kumar Talhar. Both are residents of Arnia.During questioning, the accused allegedly confessed their links with Pakistan-based handlers and admitted to having received two air-dropped consignments in the past. Information obtained from the duo led cops to a third suspect, also named Ajay Kumar. He was arrested with 464g of opium resin and 13.3g of heroin, police said.Further probe revealed the involvement of a fourth suspect—Jaganpreet Randhawa alias Jaggi, believed to be a forward link in the smuggling nexus—who was arrested in Punjab.Arnia PS registered an FIR under relevant sections of the NDPS and Arms Acts. Officials said further investigation was underway.Many such cases have earlier been reported from forward areas along the Indo-Pak international border and the Line of Control in J&K. The probes were later handed over to NIA due to the magnitude of the smuggled contraband, arms and ammunition.
Article Summary: J&K Police have arrested four suspects, including one from Punjab, in connection with the alleged cross-border smuggling of drugs and arms via drones. An Italy- made Beretta pistol, two magazines, four live rounds, and over 1kg of narcotics were seized during subsequent searches.
